title: Design System: Giáo trình kể bằng tiếng nói

display.purpose: Episode title only, rising from behind the orange rule on the title scene.

headline.purpose: The single plum line of a question scene.

title.purpose: Shared heading across bullets, formula, outro; 700/40px variant above a diagram.

body.purpose: Bullet lines, capped at 78% measure in landscape.

caption.purpose: Burned-in karaoke subtitle, present on every frame.

secondary.purpose: Subtitles, scene captions, diagram sub-labels, hints.

label.purpose: Uppercase chapter head and episode/part label in the top corners.

shadows.name: node-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Applied to code-drawn diagram node groups and enclosure groups. Never to arrows, labels, text, quoted slide rasters, or frame furniture.

motion.name: frame-in
motion.purpose: Every scene's content fades up over 10 frames; paper and furniture never fade.

motion.name: frame-out
motion.purpose: Content fades out over the last 8 frames of a scene.

motion.name: spring-settled
motion.purpose: Default entrance for title, heading, bullets, image, quote, outro, diagram steps.

motion.name: spring-interject
motion.purpose: Question scene only, scaling 0.965 to 1 like someone cutting in.

motion.name: build-window
motion.purpose: Staggered build window for bullet lines and diagram steps; the remainder holds still under the narration.

motion.name: image-drift
motion.purpose: Slow push on a quoted slide raster so a static figure stays alive.

components.name: Running Head
components.description: Persistent frame furniture: chapter title left, episode or part label right, inset by the page margin.
components.css: .ds-runhead { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 22px; letter-spacing: 3px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6B6054; background: #F5F1EC; padding: 24px 160px; } .ds-runhead-right { letter-spacing: 2px; }

components.name: Progress Rail
components.description: 3px full-bleed rail at the bottom edge of every frame; accent fill shows episode progress, plum on an ask scene.
components.css: .ds-rail { height: 3px; width: 100%; background: #DED5C8; } .ds-rail-fill { height: 100%; width: 42%; background: #C8613C; } .ds-rail.ds-rail-ask .ds-rail-fill { background: #7E4F63; }

components.name: Caption Band
components.description: Always-on karaoke subtitle. Spoken words ink at 700, unspoken soft ink at 500 — weight and hue, never opacity.
components.html: Service là một thành phần độc lập, gọi qua mạng.
components.css: .ds-captions { display: flex; justify-content: center; padding: 0 160px; background: #F5F1EC; } .ds-captions-line { font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 36px; line-height: 1.35; text-align: center; max-width: 68%; } .ds-cap-spoken { color: #2B2520; font-weight: 700; } .ds-cap-ahead { color: #6B6054; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Bullet Line
components.description: A bullet row: accent numeral in a narrow gutter, body line capped at 78% measure. Lines stagger in from the left across 62% of the scene.
components.html:
1

Service độc lập với bên gọi nó: triển khai riêng, phiên bản riêng.
components.css: .ds-bullet { display: flex; gap: 26px; align-items: baseline; background: #F5F1EC; padding: 15px 0; } .ds-bullet-num { font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 38px; font-weight: 700; color: #C8613C; min-width: 32px; } .ds-bullet-text { font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 40px; line-height: 1.35; color: #2B2520; margin: 0; max-width: 78%; }

components.description: A code-drawn figure node. Filled with page paper so it reads as cut from the sheet; the only element allowed to lift off the paper.

components.description: The focal node — the one the narration is on. Accent wash fill, accent stroke and lettering. Exactly one per figure.

components.name: Diagram Enclosure
components.description: Groups nodes into one named system. Deep-paper fill, hairline rule stroke, right-aligned soft-ink label at the bottom inside edge.

components.name: Verb Chip
components.description: Solid accent chip carrying an HTTP verb in paper-coloured 800; the one place the accent becomes a fill.
components.css: .ds-chip-verb { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 190px; height: 66px; border-radius: 12px; background: #C8613C; color: #F5F1EC; font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 800; }

components.name: Slide Quotation
components.description: A verbatim raster from the course deck: keeps the slide's cyan and letterform, lies flat, white ground dissolved by multiply blend, captioned with its source slide.
components.css: .ds-quote-slide { margin: 0; text-align: center; background: #F5F1EC; } .ds-quote-slide img { max-width: 100%; max-height: 56vh; object-fit: contain; mix-blend-mode: multiply; box-shadow: none; border: none; } .ds-quote-slide figcaption { font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', sans-serif; font-size: 28px; color: #6B6054; margin-top: 34px; }

components.name: Question Scene
components.description: The second speaker's state: the whole sheet turns rose, the headline is plum, the rail tints plum. No border, no badge.

narrative.northStar: The Printed Textbook Page, Read Aloud
narrative.overview:
Every frame is a page of a warm-paper textbook with a lecturer's voice over it. Wide margins, ink on cream, one earth-orange accent used as a pointer, and figures that sit on the page like book illustrations rather than screenshots pasted onto a slide. The genre default — bullets drifting on a dark background, every scene arriving with the same fade, glow and grid — is rejected outright: here each scene type has its own entrance, and the figure is the protagonist, not decoration.

Density is low and deliberate. One idea per frame, at most four bullets, 15–45 seconds of speech, and a caption band that is always lit because most of the audience watches muted on a phone. The only persistent furniture is a running chapter head top-left, an episode/part label top-right, and a 3px progress rail hugging the bottom edge — the rail is the series' recognition mark.

There is no hover, focus, or keyboard vocabulary in this system. State means two things only: which scene type is on screen, and who is speaking. The second speaker ("ask") swaps the whole paper to a rose-tinted sheet and tints the rail plum instead of drawing a coloured border.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper, brown-black ink, no neutral grey anywhere.
One accent (earth orange) used as a pointer, never as a fill field.
Scene-specific entrances; a shared 10-frame in, 8-frame out on the frame itself.
A burned-in karaoke caption on every single frame.
Two frame sizes, one layout: 1920×1080 and 1080×1920 from the same components.

rules.name: The No Neutral Grey Rule
rules.body: Every soft tone is a warm brown drawn from the ink family. Any value with equal R/G/B is out of world.

rules.name: The Pointer Accent Rule
rules.body: Earth orange marks one thing at a time: a numeral, a rule, a single focal node, the rail's progress. It is never the background of a block of text.

rules.name: The Speaker-Is-Paper Rule
rules.body: A speaker change is expressed by swapping the sheet (#F7EBE6) and the rail tint. Never by a coloured left border, never by a badge.

rules.name: The Citation Hue Rule
rules.body: A slide-quoted raster keeps the course deck's cyan and its own letterform. That foreign hue is a declared citation, not a palette break.

rules.name: The 32px Floor Rule
rules.body: No running text below the equivalent of 32px at 1080p; the caption band sits at 36px because the audience is on a phone.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Opacity Rule
rules.body: Caption cueing is colour plus weight (ink/700 vs soft ink/500). Nothing in the caption band is ever faded with opacity.

rules.name: The Whole-Clause Rule
rules.body: Captions advance a clause at a time, broken on sentence and clause punctuation, up to 18 words landscape / 14 portrait — never a fixed N-word window that would split a term across cues.

rules.name: The No Raw Pixel Rule
rules.body: Nothing writes a pixel size directly. Every size, margin and gap goes through useLayout() — s() for type and spacing, the padX/padTop/caption* fractions for structure. This is what makes the portrait cut compose rather than shrink. The only literals in the build are the 3px rail, the 4px title rule, SVG geometry inside a diagram's own viewBox, and the 1.72 portrait multiplier itself.

rules.name: The Caption Reserve Rule
rules.body: The bottom 18–22% of every frame belongs to the caption band. Layouts fill the column above it; nothing is centred against the raw frame height.

rules.name: The One Lifted Surface Rule
rules.body: Only diagram nodes and enclosures carry shadow. Arrows, labels, headings, captions, quoted slide rasters and the frame furniture all lie flat on the paper. There are no cards, no panels, no glass, no glow.

rules.name: The Hairline Structure Rule
rules.body: Horizontal division is a 2px rule in #DED5C8 spanning the text column — never a boxed container, never a filled band.

rules.name: The Diagram Provenance Rule
rules.body: A diagram scene is redrawn in the series palette and lifts off the paper with the node shadow. An image scene is a verbatim quotation from the course slides: it keeps the slide's cyan and letterform, lies flat with no shadow, has its white ground removed with mix-blend-mode: multiply, and must carry a caption naming the source slide. Students have to recognise the same figure when they reopen the deck; the foreign hue is a declared citation, not a palette break. Never recolour a quoted slide into the house palette, and never redraw a figure without also moving it into the house palette.

rules.name: The Figure-First Rule
rules.body: When a scene's point is a structure, it is a diagram or image scene — not a bullet list describing the structure.

dos: Do route every size, margin, gap and radius through useLayout() (s(), padX, padTop, captionBottom, captionWidth) so the 1080×1920 cut recomposes instead of shrinking.
Do give each new scene type its own entrance and its own spring, in the existing 18–26 frame band.
Do keep the caption band lit on every frame and leave the bottom 18–22% of the frame clear for it.
Do express a speaker change as a paper swap to #F7EBE6 plus a plum rail.
Do caption every quoted slide raster with the slide it came from, and let it keep the deck's cyan.
Do fill diagram nodes with page paper so they read as cut from the sheet, and reserve the accent tone for the single node the narration is on.
Do read scene length from the audio manifest; a scene's duration is its audio plus the tail.
donts: Don't write a literal pixel value in a component. The exceptions are already in the build (3px rail, 4px title rule, SVG geometry inside a diagram viewBox) and the list does not grow.
Don't introduce neutral grey, gradients, glass, glow, grid overlays, or a dark background — the warm-paper world is pinned by the user.
Don't put a shadow on anything but a diagram node or enclosure group, and never a hard offset shadow: the one allowed shadow is soft, downward, and ink-tinted.
Don't recolour or restyle a quoted slide raster into the house palette, and don't wrap it in a white card — mix-blend-mode: multiply is how its ground disappears.
Don't mark a speaker, a scene type, or an emphasis with a thick coloured left border or a badge.
Don't cue captions with opacity, and don't cut them on a fixed word count mid-term.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow line above a heading. The uppercase running head is frame furniture at the top corners; it is not a licence for eyebrows inside the content column.
Don't add a second type family. Be Vietnam Pro at 400/600/800 covers the whole ramp; KaTeX's math face is tolerated inside formula math only.
Don't hardcode durationInFrames in a component or hand-edit manifest.json.
